summary: Contains two corrections to RFC 2533, which defined a syntax for describing media feature sets: one fixes an error in the formal syntax and the other fixes a problem in the text. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: This is an errata sheet. It fixes two mistakes in an earlier rule book about describing what a device can display.

questions: what is a media feature set
subtitle: Two small fixes to the media feature set syntax and matching rules of RFC 2533.

tldr.problem: RFC 2533 describes media feature capabilities with feature expressions, but contained an error in its formal syntax and an error in its matching reduction rules.
tldr.mechanism: This memo corrects the 'setentry' grammar production, replacing a literal '/' with an alternative, and completes one incomplete rewriting rule for the unordered value comparison (LE f a) (GE f b).
tldr.outcome: The syntax fix affects the normative content of RFC 2533; the rule fix affects non-normative content.

today: RFC 2738 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2533. The unit metadata shows nothing obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: What Is Being Corrected
sections.content:
RFC 2533 presents an expression format for describing media feature capabilities with simple media feature tags. It lets message handling agents describe what content they can handle, and gives an algorithm for finding the common capabilities of two feature expressions.

This memo makes two corrections. One fixes the formal syntax specification, which affects normative content. The other fixes the rules for reducing feature comparison predicates in the matching algorithm, which affects non-normative content. It uses ABNF as described in RFC 2234.
sections.eli5: A rule book for describing what a device can show had two mistakes, and this note fixes them.

sections.title: Correction to the Set Syntax
sections.content:
Section 4.1 of RFC 2533 defined a set expression with the production setentry = value "/" range. It should read setentry = value / range. The '/' is not a character literal; it separates two alternative forms, a single value or a range.

The corrected grammar allows the set examples in section 4.2.5 of RFC 2533, such as ( width=[3,4,6..17/2] ).
sections.eli5: A slash was meant to mean 'or' but was written as a letter to type. Fixing it lets lists mix single numbers and ranges.

sections.title: Correction to the Matching Rules
sections.content:
Section 5.8.2 of RFC 2533 lists rewriting rules for simplifying comparisons with unordered values. The second rule, for (LE f a) (GE f b), said only FALSE when a and b differ. It should read: (LE f a) when a=b, and FALSE otherwise.

A note says implementation experience suggested a revised matching algorithm with more useful simplification rules. Apart from this change, the RFC 2533 algorithm was implemented and shown to work, though results are not always in the most convenient form. A revised algorithm is planned to be tested and published later.

Security considerations are those of RFC 2533 and related documents.
sections.eli5: One rule only said what to do when two numbers differ. The fix adds what to do when they are the same.

data.title: setentry in ABNF
data.code:
Old:       setentry = value "/" range
Corrected: setentry = value / range

references.text: Klyne, G., "A Syntax for Describing Media Feature Sets", RFC 2533, March 1999.
Crocker, D. and P. Overell, "Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications: ABNF", RFC 2234, November 1997.
